title: Copper wire theft shuts down Eugene-area 911 lines for nine hours, police warn of risks

 EUGENE, Ore. — A copper wire theft that knocked out 911 phone service for nine hours in Eugene is prompting police to warn that what may look like a small property crime can disrupt essential services, cost thousands of dollars and put lives at risk.
 Eugene police said the theft happened at 6:35 a.m. Nov. 8 at West Second Avenue near Chambers Street, disabling all phone communications to the Central Lane Communications Center, which serves about 250,000 people in Lane County. During the outage, residents were instructed to text 911 in an emergency. Police said a couple of phone lines were restored later in the morning but only in a limited capacity, and other callers were rerouted to outside agencies, causing delays of as much as three to five minutes per call.
 Police said phone lines were not fully restored until 3:30 p.m., and the outage affected hundreds of people who needed emergency assistance.
 Dean Daniel Bryan, 26, was arrested Nov. 11 on two counts of first-degree criminal mischief and two counts of second-degree theft, according to the Eugene Police Department. Police said Bryan admitted to the thefts and told investigators he generally strips wires and sells the copper to local metal recyclers for $5 per pound.
 Police said Bryan cut a bundle of 600 wires. The value of the wires and connectors was estimated at about $100, but the financial impact of repairs by Century Link Telecommunication was estimated at $5,000. Police said the wire stolen from the West Second Avenue location was estimated to have generated less than $50 if sold.
 Security camera video showed Bryan committing the theft, then squeezing through a locked gate of a nearby business as he appeared to hide from responding police, according to police. Investigators said he ditched the wire in the bed of one of the business’ service trucks parked in the lot before walking away while pushing his bike. Detectives located the video Wednesday, Nov. 11, identified the suspect and made the arrest, police said.
 Eugene police said the case underscores broader concerns about copper thefts, which can interrupt emergency communications, disable traffic signals, leave public pathways without lighting and create dangerous conditions for residents and first responders.
 Police also directed a warning to scrap metal dealers, recyclers and others purchasing copper wire to verify where materials come from. Police noted Oregon law requires scrap metal businesses to maintain transaction records and comply with identification and reporting requirements, and that businesses that knowingly purchase stolen materials or disregard legal requirements may face criminal consequences. Police said they will continue investigating copper thefts, including the circumstances surrounding the sale and purchase of stolen materials.
 Police asked residents and businesses to report suspicious activity around utility boxes, telecommunications lines, construction sites and other critical infrastructure. Anyone witnessing a theft in progress should call 911. Information about previously occurring thefts can be reported to Eugene Police at 541-682-5111.
